correctness.rationale: The unique inward common-circle intersection for a side of length at most 2 is explicit. Its two affine coordinates lie in [0,1] exactly under the asserted inequalities; both side types together leave exactly one feasible vertex-only triple, which is explicitly omitted. At fixed angle with \(c\ge\tfrac12\) the separate side constraints force the sharp rhombus. At \(c\le\tfrac12\) a convex-quadratic endpoint bound for \(k\ge3\) proves the sharp, uniquely attained rhombus except for the forbidden 60-degree endpoint. The checker directly corroborated 720 geometric membership tests, 222 feasible perimeter cells, and exact exceptional cases. The all-real statement follows from the analytic proof, not the finite grid.

value.rationale: This is the complete geometric membership and sharp fixed-angle optimization for the natural centrally symmetric quadrilateral case of a published side-strut perimeter problem. It exhibits a sharp geometric 60-degree regime boundary with nonattainment due to the nonvertex definition, identifies uniquely optimal rhombi at every other angle, and determines the unique global square minimizer. The specific invariant is pre-motivated by the published general-polygon question; it is not a random finite slice or mere change of notation.
